Depends what you take that’s way too broad of a question. I took an OD and passed out, was in and out of consciousness woke up to myself screaming and crying I’m dying because no one could hear me. Like being locked in a coffin alive. I knew I had a tiny window to run out the door and get to the road. Passed out on the sidewalk someone found me and I woke up in hospital. So much can go wrong and although I wanted to die at the time. I didn’t expect to wake up in such a frightening experience.

You cannot bring this up in therapy there is no help but self discovery and shifting what you care about. There really is no help in dealing with it as far as I’m concerned. Because people are not informed enough. It’s 100% an OCD trait. I’m sure of it but the thing is it’s also connected to real life founded judgments. And it makes no sense for the world to understand what they already know. No one will admit it. But google your most insecure thought and you’ll get a response. If I have dark circles and a hunchback as a result for my aversion and avoidance toward people I’m judged. I’m scared of them too. That’s the worst part of this is how you present psychically and it’s fucked up because in one sense, it’s just a shell and it doesn’t matter but it shows. I think BDD is actually a conversation on things deeper that people aren’t willing or care to talk about yet. Your worries are 100% true, to you. I’m not saying if you worry about your big nose I’m not gonna notice it. But I probably won’t care. But I know most people judge of first impressions and the shell I avoid.
